description: Final ownership disposition for every symbol the active PMFreak graph imported from the former src/aoc/protocol and src/aoc/enterprise pseudo-upstream trees.

symbols.notes: Deprecated-alias rule applied: NOT adopted. Upstream reaches this name only through an alias upstream itself marks @deprecated, pointing at ExecutionAuthorizationProvider — a single canonical-request method returning AdapterResult<…>. PMFreak’s port is a four-method domain surface (requireWorkspaceMembership, requireProjectPermission, requireGovernancePermission, requireAgentScope) that throws GovernanceAccessDeniedError rather than returning a result envelope: different method surface, different error model, different failure semantics. The port expresses a PMFreak application need over Supabase membership/RBAC/agent-scope tables, so it stays PMFreak-owned; PmfreakAccessVerificationAdapter remains its implementation.
No public upstream export. PMFreak agent-token verification need (signature, replay protection, revocation, scope binding). Implemented by PmfreakAgentAttestationAdapter.
Proven identical: `export type AgentId = string` on both sides. Same proof as WorkspaceId. Strategy C1.

Strategy C2 (persistence projection renamed). Different categories of object entirely: PMFreak is a persisted ai_agent_scopes row (id, agent_id, workspace_id, resource_type, resource_id, permission, status, expires_at); upstream AgentScope is `readonly string[]`. Not mapped by name. No canonical AgentScope is derived anywhere in the active graph, so no mapper was invented.

No upstream owner (the upstream ProtocolError family is a different hierarchy). PMFreak-owned denial error carrying a structured `context.reason`. Class and its `name` property renamed together; verified safe because every consumer discriminates by `instanceof` and reads `context.reason`/`message` — no code path reads `.name` (the only `.name` checks in the repo are for AbortError/TimeoutError) and the route error boundary returns fixed generic codes, never the error name. Denial outcomes unchanged.

No upstream owner, publicly or privately. PMFreak’s own actor descriptor for policy evaluation (actorId, actorType, workspaceId, projectId, roles, permissions). Renamed to name the bounded context rather than to strip a substring.
No upstream owner. String alias carrying PMFreak workspace role names ("owner","admin","PM","external_stakeholder"), used for approval routing only, never for permission evaluation.

No upstream owner. Merged with its own downstream alias: governance-core previously declared `type GovernanceAction = AocGovernanceAction`, so the two names always denoted one type. The duplicate declaration is removed and the PMFreak-owned name is the single definition. Route action values ("project.read","ai.execute",...) unchanged.

No upstream owner. Merged with its own downstream alias exactly as AocGovernanceAction was. Decision values ("allow","deny","require_human_approval","require_admin_approval","require_additional_scope") unchanged.

No upstream owner. This is PMFreak’s persisted audit event vocabulary ("governance_action_allowed","denied_permission","project_scope_violation",...). Type renamed; every member string value left byte-identical because these values are written to the audit store.
No upstream owner. PMFreak workspace RBAC permission vocabulary consumed by GOVERNANCE_POLICY_REGISTRY.requiredPermission and checked against ROLE_PERMISSION_MAP. Member values unchanged.

No upstream owner. Renamed for semantic honesty, not merely to drop the prefix: its only consumer is GovernancePolicy.riskLevel and the emitted decision riskLevel field. It never expressed a trust level. Member values ("low","medium","high","critical") unchanged.

Strategy C2. PMFreak is the snake_case persisted audit row (created_at, event_type, actor_user_id, actor_agent_id, event_detail, open index signature); upstream is a camelCase readonly canonical envelope (eventId, emittedAt, occurredAt, actorId, subject, correlationId, reasonCodes, payload). Persistence representation vs canonical contract. No historical audit record altered and no conversion invented — nothing in the active graph emits a canonical envelope. The existing PMFreak API-layer alias AuditTimelineItem is preserved at the consumer bridge.
No upstream claim-signing port bundle exists. Aggregates the four ports PMFreak claim issuance and verification require (trustDomain, trustCoordination, securityAudit, signer). Kept PMFreak-owned.

Strategy C2. Upstream CapabilityGrant is an alias of CapabilityToken — a signed, self-describing token with schemaVersion, issuer, subject, resource, scope, constraints, proof. PMFreak persists a capability_grants row (id, workspace_id, capability_request_id, permission, target_resource_type, target_resource_id, status, expires_at). Structurally and semantically different; the PMFreak record must not carry the canonical name. Stored columns unchanged.

Strategy C4 (distinct concept, NO_EQUIVALENCE). PMFreak values are bare permission codes persisted in capability_requests.requested_permission, capability_grants.permission, ai_agent_scopes.permission and delegations.permission ("read","write","approve","manage","execute","delegate","write_memory",...). Upstream is a namespaced governance capability vocabulary ("resource:read","governance:approve",...). No total mapping exists in either direction: upstream has no counterpart for "manage"/"delegate" as PMFreak means them, and PMFreak has no counterpart for "audit:export"/"consent"-scoped values. No conversion invented; no external governance boundary in the active graph requires one. Renamed so the name no longer implies the canonical vocabulary. Stored values unchanged.

Strategy C2. PMFreak is the snake_case capability_requests storage row; upstream is a camelCase contract with a wider status vocabulary (adds "expired","consumed"). Storage, domain and wire representations kept separate; no database columns changed in this increment.

Strategy C4 (distinct concept, NO_EQUIVALENCE). PMFreak resource vocabulary is product-specific: "operational_memory", "ai_coprocess", "copilot", "governance_object" have no canonical counterpart; upstream carries "document","dataset","policy","consent","delegation","audit_log","memory","execution","integration" which PMFreak does not persist. Only "workspace" and "project" coincide. Not added to Protocol; not coerced onto an unrelated canonical resource. Stored values unchanged.
No upstream counterpart. Projects a claim into PMFreak audit metadata; emitted key names are preserved because they are written to the audit store.

No upstream owner. Writes the governance_approval_requests row through the privileged-DB port under the documented PRIVILEGED_ACCESS/AUDIT_REF annotations. Payload keys, upsert conflict target and 24h expiry preserved byte-identically; this is PMFreak persistence and confirms the layer was never upstream’s.

Upstream ships CAPABILITY_CLAIM_VERSION but no signing surface, so no canonical operation exists to adopt and none was invented. PMFreak implementation retained and moved. It already consumes the canonical packaged artifact for serialization (canonicalizeJSON from @aoc/protocol/canonical) — that import is preserved unchanged, which is what keeps signatures over already-stored claims byte-identical. All claim version strings, the "aoc-local" default trust domain and the deprecated pmfreak-capability-claim-v* accepted values are left untouched because they are persisted and must stay verifiable.

Strategy C2. Upstream Delegation is a four-field chain-policy descriptor embedded in a CapabilityToken (delegator, chainDepth, maxDepth, allowedReDelegation). PMFreak persists a full delegations lifecycle row (delegator/delegatee actor identity split across user and agent columns, source grant, parent delegation, delegated_scope, status, delegation_depth, expiry, revocation). Related lifecycles at different layers, not the same concept; no silent alias. Stored columns unchanged.

Renamed with its sibling for the same reason. Frontera does export enforceEnforcementPipeline, but over the AuthorizationGrantInput contract above; the closest behavioural counterpart is orchestrateAuthorization, which is also differently shaped. PMFreak’s function composes a runtime context and runs PMFreak governance enforcement including approval-request persistence.
No upstream owner. Evaluate-then-persist-approval wrapper. Behavior unchanged.

Renamed to remove the most dangerous collision in the inventory: the canonical Frontera export has the identical name and arity but a different contract — upstream is (input: AuthorizationGrantInput {requestId, actorId, capability: CapabilityToken, consentGrants, access, tenantId, orgId}, deps: AuthorizationOrchestrationDeps) => Promise<{allowed, reasonCodes, audit}>, verified directly against the installed artifact; PMFreak’s is (input: GovernanceEvaluationInput {routeId, action, actorType, workspace/project scope}, options: ComposeRuntimeContextOptions) => the PMFreak governance decision with decisionId, trace, riskLevel and approval routing. Two-argument shape coincidence made a silent mis-binding possible; the rename removes it.
No upstream owner. PMFreak governance evaluation pipeline. Body unchanged apart from renamed type references; guard order, denial reasons, approval routing and audit emission preserved exactly.
No upstream owner. Human-readable rendering of a PMFreak governance decision. Output string format unchanged.

No upstream owner. The route-level authority table mapping each PMFreak governance action to required permission, allowed actor types, agent compatibility, deny event type and risk level. Byte-identical after the move; this table *is* PMFreak’s authority policy and any change to it would be an authority change.

No upstream owner. Was a re-declared alias of AocGovernanceAction; now the single canonical PMFreak declaration, re-exported from the runtime barrel so existing consumer import sites keep the same symbol name.

No upstream owner. Already PMFreak-named; only its location changes. Kept distinct from the four-member actor kind on GovernanceActorContext — this three-member type ("user","ai_agent","system") is what the policy registry gates on.
No upstream owner. Was a re-declared alias of AocGovernanceDecisionState; now the single canonical PMFreak declaration, re-exported from the runtime barrel.
No upstream owner. Persisted approval lifecycle status vocabulary. Location only; values unchanged.
No upstream owner. PMFreak route-level governance request (routeId, action, actor identity, workspace/project scope). Location only.
PMFreak implementation over the canonical serialization profile. SHA-256 over canonicalize(claim); claim hashes are persisted and used for revocation lookup, so the algorithm and input are unchanged.

Strategy C4 (distinct lifecycle, NO_EQUIVALENCE). Upstream PolicyDecision is a three-state policy verdict ("allow","deny","conditional"). PMFreak persists a five-state *evaluation outcome*: "allow","deny","require_approval","expired","no_match". "require_approval" is a PMFreak workflow state that routes into governance_approval_requests and is not the same as upstream "conditional" (which carries no approval routing); "expired" and "no_match" are evaluator outcomes, not policy verdicts, and have no upstream member at all. Collapsing five states onto three would lose the approval-routing and no-match distinctions, so the states were not collapsed. The two local duplicate declarations were deduplicated into one PMFreak definition. Stored values unchanged; mapLegacyPolicyDecision still fails closed to "deny".
Not publicly exported upstream. Input contract of the PMFreak-owned PolicyEvaluatorPort, carrying PMFreak concerns (rbacAllowed, requestedDurationHours, justification). Stays with its port.
Not publicly exported upstream. Result contract of the PMFreak-owned PolicyEvaluatorPort; carries the five-state PMFreak outcome plus matched policy/grant provenance. Stays with its port.

Deprecated-alias rule applied: NOT adopted. Upstream counterpart PolicyDecisionProvider returns the three-state canonical PolicyDecision in an AdapterResult envelope; PMFreak’s port returns the five-state PolicyEvaluationResult including matchedPolicyIds, matchedGrantId and evaluatedAt, and is backed by PMFreak policy/grant tables. Incompatible outcome vocabulary and result shape.

No upstream persistence port exists at all. PMFreak service-role Supabase access behind an explicit, audited context (routeId, operation, reason, systemActor). Squarely PMFreak infrastructure; keeping it is correct dependency inversion. Its associated types AocPrivilegedDbContext/AocDbClient are renamed PrivilegedDbContext/PrivilegedDbClient.
Proven identical: `export type ProjectId = string` on both sides. Same proof as WorkspaceId. Strategy C1.
No public upstream export. Emission port for PMFreak’s own audit vocabulary and payload shape; persists into PMFreak audit tables. Kept PMFreak-owned.

Deprecated-alias rule applied: NOT adopted. PMFreak’s getRevocationReason resolves revocation across four correlated identifiers at once (keyId, claimHash, delegationId, grantId) and returns a reason string or null; the upstream RevocationLookup alias is differently shaped. Revocation is a fail-closed PMFreak concern backed by PMFreak tables.

Deprecated-alias rule applied: NOT adopted. PMFreak’s port is a seven-method signing-key lifecycle surface (getActiveSigningKey, getActiveAsymmetricSigningKey, resolveVerificationKey, resolvePublicVerificationKey, verifyIssuerTrust, evaluateVerifierPolicy, resolveHmacSecret — the last synchronous and env/vault-backed). The upstream provider exposes a single canonical-request method. Host secret resolution deliberately stays on the PMFreak side of the boundary.

Proven identical: `export type WorkspaceId = string` on both sides. Plain alias, not branded; no optionality, nullability or serialization difference; no runtime constructor. Publicly exported via contracts/index.d.ts `export type * from "./legacy-contracts"`. Not marked @deprecated. Strategy C1.
